clue.text: Drinks from abroad brought back out of date

blocks.note: a cat laps milk: it drinks
de is French for 'from', so a foreign 'from'

explanation.surface: Imported beverages have been sent back because they are past their sell-by date.
explanation.walkthrough: The French word de, read backwards, sits after LAPS to give LAPSED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lapsed has expired, like a passport or subscription no longer valid.

clue.text: Leak from sauce – I suggest we put on top

indicators.note: in a down entry, putting one piece on top means it comes first, above the other piece

blocks.note: 'let's' is how one suggests doing something together

explanation.walkthrough: Sauce here is impudence, not a condiment.

clue.text: One has no faith in Harry returning to support father

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word for harry is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: pa is an informal word for father
to harry someone is to nag them

explanation.surface: Someone loses faith when Harry comes back to help his dad.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry looks like a name but is the verb to pester.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagan is a heathen, someone outside the main religions and so regarded as without faith.

clue.text: Very old vehicle avoiding motorway

indicators.note: avoiding something means keeping clear of it, so that letter is left out of the vehicle

blocks.note: ex means former
a tram is a vehicle on rails
M is the motorway abbreviation, as in the M1

explanation.surface: A vintage car stays off the motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra as an adverb intensifies, as in 'extra careful', meaning especially or very.

clue.text: This first lady’s wearing trousers

definitions.note: read as a plural noun: people who trouser, pocketing what is not theirs

indicators.note: the lady is wearing the first word as clothing, so it wraps around her

blocks.note: taken as written
Eve was the first woman in Genesis

explanation.surface: A president's wife is pictured in trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trousers' looks like clothing but is a verb turned into a noun: to trouser is to pocket money dishonestly.
explanation.definitionFit: To trouser money is slang for stealing it, so those who trouser are thieves.

clue.text: Left boot restricting Pole

blocks.note: to boot is to kick, to toe

explanation.walkthrough: Pole has a capital to suggest a Polish person; it is a wooden spar.

clue.text: Note cocked up by Muse, blowing No.1 from Taylor Swift

blowing in the sense of squandering or losing, so that letter goes

the opening letter

clue.text: Change ending to composition after failing the other way round

verse is poetic composition

explanation.walkthrough: VERSE becomes VERSA by swapping its last letter E for A.

clue.text: Polished United halfway through hit the back of the net

indicators.note: placed halfway through means set into the middle of the other word

blocks.clueFragment: hit the back of the net
blocks.note: in football you have scored when the ball hits the back of the net
U is the standard abbreviation for United in team names

explanation.surface: A slick United side netted a goal midway through the match.
explanation.walkthrough: Polished reads as describing United's play, but it is the definition, meaning rubbed clean.
explanation.definitionFit: Scoured means scrubbed hard until clean and shiny, so a scoured pan has been polished.

clue.text: King leaving dignified greeting for old leader

indicators.note: the king is leaving, so his letter departs from the phrase

blocks.note: R stands for rex, Latin for king
grand means stately, dignified
hi is an informal greeting

explanation.surface: A king walks out on a stately welcome laid on for a former leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahatma Gandhi led India's independence movement and died in 1948, a historical figure and so an old leader.

clue.text: They’re reluctant to part with bread, even rolls

definitions.text: They’re reluctant to part with bread

blocks.note: a tight contest is an even one
a wad is a roll of banknotes

explanation.surface: Some people won't share their loaves, not even the bread rolls.
explanation.walkthrough: Bread is slang for money, and rolls are wads of notes, not baked goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Tightwads are misers, stingy people who hate spending money, which is slang bread.

clue.text: Masculine couple in the auditorium linked to Oscar

indicators.note: an auditorium is where an audience listens, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: a couple is a match, a pair suited to each other

explanation.definitionFit: Macho describes aggressively manly behaviour, an exaggerated show of being masculine.

clue.text: Guy‘s path cut by three feet

indicators.note: a cut word is trimmed, losing its final letter

blocks.note: a lane is a narrow path
a yard is three feet

clue.text: East End labourer finished in southern town

blocks.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand
over means ended

clue.text: Show worker taken on by scandal-hit organisation suggestive gestures

indicators.note: an organisation that takes someone on employs them, holding them inside it

a worker ant
mime is acting by gesture alone

explanation.walkthrough: PO is the Post Office, the UK postal service whose Horizon computer scandal was a major news story.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantomime is a British Christmas stage show, a comic family entertainment.

clue.text: Local area bishop’s breaking record

indicators.note: breaking into a word means splitting it and sitting inside the gap

blocks.note: a local is a native of a place
A is a standard abbreviation for area
RR is Right Reverend, a bishop's title

explanation.surface: A district's bishop is smashing a record.
explanation.walkthrough: ARR goes in after the first letter of NATIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrative is an account of events, something that records what happened.

clue.text: All things considered, no flipping money left!

indicators.note: flipping something turns it over, so the short word is read backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
the balance is the money remaining in an account

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry on finding the account is empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a mild British swear word, but it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: On balance is an idiom for after weighing everything up, having considered all the factors.

clue.text: Sky media top dog giving broadcast

blocks.note: the sky is the air above
ED is short for editor, the boss of a newspaper

explanation.surface: The head of the Sky media company puts out a programme.
explanation.walkthrough: Sky looks like the TV company, which fits the media surface; it is the air.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme that has been aired has been transmitted on radio or television.

clue.text: Drop clean brush

blocks.note: first meaning: cancel or abandon a plan
second meaning: wash by rubbing hard
third meaning: low scrubby vegetation, brushwood

explanation.walkthrough: Three separate meanings of one word, not two; brush is the undergrowth sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The word can mean cancel a plan, wash vigorously, or stunted trees and bushes covering land.

clue.text: Discontinue the Telegraph, put up while away

indicators.note: put up means raised, and in a down entry raising a word reads it upwards

blocks.note: the setter's newspaper speaking of itself
to while away time is to spend it

explanation.surface: A reader cancels the paper while on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: The Telegraph, where this puzzle appears, refers to itself as us.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspend something is to halt it for a time, so discontinue is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Clement Attlee ultimately slashes what a stand-in worker is paid

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the name is kept
a letter that slashes through a phrase cuts into it and sits inside

blocks.clueFragment: what a stand-in worker is paid
blocks.note: a temp's rate of pay
the last letter

explanation.surface: The post-war prime minister Clement Attlee cuts temporary staff wages.
explanation.walkthrough: Clement looks like Attlee's first name, making the surface about the post-war Labour leader; it is the adjective meaning mild.
explanation.definitionFit: Clement weather is mild and pleasant, which is what a temperate climate is.

clue.text: Checks short article on Tube travelling north

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the last letter of the article is dropped
travelling north in a down entry means reading upwards

blocks.note: the definite article
a drinking straw is a tube

explanation.surface: A brief newspaper piece about the London Underground heading north.
explanation.walkthrough: Tube looks like the London Underground; it is a straw.
explanation.definitionFit: To thwart is to block or frustrate, and to check someone is likewise to stop their progress.

clue.text: Publication one abandons after the setter reveals character

indicators.note: the single letter abandons the word, walking out of it
after places the shortened publication behind the setter

blocks.note: the setter referring to themself
a title is a published book or magazine
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A magazine dropped by one person shows what the compiler is made of.
explanation.definitionFit: Mettle is spirit and strength of character, the courage to face a challenge.

clue.text: Volunteers discovered tent is at an angle

indicators.note: dis-covered means with its cover taken off, so the outside letters are stripped

blocks.note: the inner letters
a ship that lists leans at an angle

explanation.surface: Helpers find a tent that has been pitched crooked.
explanation.walkthrough: Discovered is read as un-covered, not as found.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlist is to sign up for service, and one who volunteers does so of their own accord.

clue.text: Terms for bus/coach permit somewhat lacking in substance

indicators.note: terms are terminals, the end points, so the final letter of each word is used

blocks.note: the final letter of each of the two words
to permit is to allow

explanation.surface: The conditions of a bus or coach pass are rather thin.
explanation.walkthrough: Terms looks like conditions of a ticket; it means ends of words.
explanation.definitionFit: A shallow argument or person lacks depth, so is somewhat short on substance.

clue.text: Year to replace old, current stock

indicators.note: one letter is put in place of another in the following word

blocks.note: Y is the abbreviation for year
O is the abbreviation for old
topical means current, of present interest

explanation.surface: A new year's goods take the place of old merchandise.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the O in TOPICAL for a Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Stock as an adjective means standard or routine, as in a stock answer, which is typical.

clue.text: Talk about hearts, mine being superior

blocks.note: a pit is a mine
C is circa, Latin for about
H for hearts, the card suit

explanation.surface: A speech about love, with my own feelings being the best.
explanation.walkthrough: Mine looks like a possessive; it is a coal mine.
explanation.definitionFit: A sales spiel delivered to persuade a buyer is called a pitch, so the word is a synonym for that kind of speech.

clue.text: Strongly desires to disown chancellor’s latest large black holes

indicators.note: the latest is the most recent, so the final letter of the word is taken

blocks.note: to crave is to want badly
the final letter

explanation.walkthrough: Black holes sounds like astronomy or a budget gap; here it is dark caverns.
explanation.definitionFit: Caves are large hollows in rock, dark and deep like holes.

clue.text: Expensive water displayed by Waitrose via newsletter

indicators.note: the letters are on display in the words that follow, spanning their boundaries

blocks.note: letters running across the three words

explanation.surface: A premium bottled water is advertised in a Waitrose mailing.
explanation.walkthrough: Waitrose is an upmarket British supermarket chain.
explanation.definitionFit: Evian is a French brand of bottled mineral water, pricey compared with tap water.

clue.text: Kindred spirit’s introduction initiated by corresponding

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: relative means in proportion to, corresponding
the opening letter

explanation.surface: A kindred spirit is introduced through letters.
explanation.walkthrough: Kindred spirit looks like one phrase, but the definition is just the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindred as a noun means one's family, the relatives one is related to.

clue.text: Stops drinking beer regularly after time, as presumably do these?

the second and fourth letters

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the answer, but the definition proper is the closing pointer: these people stop drinking beer.
explanation.definitionFit: People counting calories would presumably give up beer, so the clue's opening describes their habit.

clue.text: Tracks from musical failing to finish, entertaining though
